selection.rationale: Scope: the accumulated training step's execution region (project.invoke, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) together with the two DDP-reducer gradient-allreduce sites it owns and would eliminate (f833b57a373d8262a384: 12x 7,087,872-element / 28,351,488 B fp32 buckets, call d0938de87369efd500322679; 8525af72c631b94e3dd0: the last-ready 39,385,344-element / 157,541,376 B bucket holding the tied wte/lm_head, wpe and early-block gradients, call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b). This exact boundary was installed and executed by two prior trials (trial-8469963975: passed quality, coverage and math checks, rejected only on step_ms; trial-7d98173269: installed, ran and failed on a concrete quality defect), so it is a proven-coherent editable region; affected_calls lists every observed call in it. Measured facts motivating the opportunity: the original objective baseline is 53.63 ms (max-rank median; rank-1 diagnostic samples 54.87/40.49/53.63, rank-0 ~36 ms), while the wire cost of the frozen 497,759,232 B fp32 gradient payload is ~33.4-34.6 ms, measured three independent ways: aligned synthetic calibration (12x 1.99 ms + 1x 10.63 ms), the non-waiting rank in the current execution timeline (12x ~1.9 ms + 10.59 ms), and trial-8469963975's fused allreduce (33.05/33.12/33.46 ms diagnostic samples). The remaining ~10-20 ms on the max rank is in-kernel device waiting from rank-arrival skew, not transfer: the current timeline measures 3.0-3.7 ms CPU submit spread per collective (execution_timeline-1221e205 cross_rank bounds), the early rank's 28 MB kernels run at ~1.9 ms wire while the late rank's spin at 2.4-3.4 ms, and the waiting direction flips between captures (current capture: rank 0 45.61 ms vs rank 1 35.59 ms) - so reducing the max rank means absorbing skew on whichever rank is early. Concrete previous failure to repair: trial-8469963975 serialized the whole gradient set into one barrier-aligned allreduce issued only after backward (plus pack/cuda-sync/unpack on the critical path); it reached the communication floor but was rejected solely on the step-time constraint (127.07 ms median vs the 120.90 ms limit = 1.05x 115.14), because it gave up the reducer's overlap (baseline: the 13-collective pipeline runs +139.3->+185.0 ms while the 4th microbatch's backward runs ~+135->+168.4 ms, only ~16.5 ms exposed). trial-7d98173269 then kept the progressive schedule via a register_comm_hook policy but regrouped buckets into chunked grouped allreduces managed by hand-rolled per-bucket torch.futures.Future objects resolved from a .then callback; all 3 parameter settings failed deterministically and identically at a continuous step (rank-0 parameter assert, opop_adapter.py observe line 338: 37470/38597376 wte elements, max abs 8.8e-6 vs 1e-6 allowed; rank-1 SIGABRT collateral). The signature is diagnostic: both gradient checks passed first (exact cross-rank equality atol=0 and the serial-reference gradient comparison), so the final p.grad was bitwise rank-identical and reference-correct, yet the post-step wte parameter was wrong by 0.001 x ~8.8e-3 - i.e. optimizer.step() consumed wte gradient storage whose last-bucket (157 MB, ~10.6 ms) reduction result was not yet visible to the consuming stream. Since the hook's divide-by-world_size + NCCL SUM is elementwise exactly the official allreduce_hook arithmetic (bitwise identical for world_size 2), the defect class is the custom chunked future/completion management, not the math. The repair therefore keeps this region and changes the policy: per-bucket official-style future chaining (dist.all_reduce(async_op=True).get_future().then(...), no cross-bucket regrouping, no hand-resolved futures, no deferred is_last flushes) so DDP's own finalization guarantees the reduction completes before the optimizer reads p.grad, while the measured skew is absorbed CPU-side (local stream drain plus gloo control-group barrier before the synchronized backward, optionally per-flush alignment as a tunable) - gloo barriers emit no NCCL kernels, so they cost wall time but not the kernel-duration metric, and their CPU wait lands on the early rank whose wall was already paced by the late rank in the baseline. Alternatives are closed: the 25 MiB bucketing is built by the frozen adapter's prepare(); shrinking the fp32 payload is barred by exact cross-rank equality (atol=0) and the 1e-6/1e-4 reference tolerances; NCCL algorithm/protocol environment changes are provider configuration and cannot take effect after prepare() has initialized the process group; compute-kernel groups (aten::mm/addmm ~10.7 ms diagnostic) do not move the NCCL-kernel objective.
selection.hypothesis: Hypothesis (to be tested on the leased worker): replacing the region's execution policy so that (a) gradient synchronization stays the default reducer's per-bucket arithmetic and standard future chaining - installed once per process on the existing DDP wrapper, firing progressively exactly when each 25 MiB bucket becomes final during the final microbatch's backward, preserving the baseline's measured communication/compute overlap - and (b) the measured 3.0-3.7 ms rank submit skew is absorbed CPU-side (stream drain plus gloo control-group alignment before the synchronized backward, with per-collective alignment available as a tunable), reduces diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms from the 53.63 ms baseline to ~34-38 ms (wire floor ~33.4-34.6 ms = 12x ~1.9-2.0 ms + ~10.6 ms; residual = post-alignment jitter) because the early rank's NCCL kernels stop spinning inside the kernel waiting for the late rank, while step_ms stays within the 120.90 ms constraint (baseline 115.14 ms; added cost is ~0.1-0.3 ms of barrier intrinsic plus the tail of the third microbatch's backward that the stream drain exposes on the CPU, with ~29 ms of the ~34 ms wire still hidden under the remaining backward compute). The previous trial's deterministic wte parameter corruption (clean gradients, 8.8e-6 parameter error = lr x stale-vs-final gradient delta) is hypothesized to be eliminated by removing the hand-rolled chunked future management, because per-bucket official future chaining restores DDP's guaranteed completion ordering between the last bucket's allreduce and optimizer.step()'s reads. Falsification conditions: if quality fails again at continuous steps with the official chaining, the comm-hook path itself is defective on this torch 2.13.0+cu129 / NCCL 2.29.7 stack and the fallback within this same region is trial-8469963975's post-backward aligned allreduce with its serialization overhead paid down (no pack/sync/unpack, fewer alignment points) to fit under 120.90 ms; if step_ms exceeds 120.90, reduce alignment points toward the single pre-backward barrier; if the objective stays above ~40 ms, the skew is autograd-progress-driven rather than a constant offset and per-bucket alignment is required. Expected benefit: up to ~15-19 ms (30-35%) off the objective, at the cost of at most a few ms of step wall time.

selection.rationale: Scope: the accumulated training step's execution region (project.invoke, call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0) together with the two DDP-reducer gradient-allreduce sites it contains and would eliminate (d0938de87369efd500322679: 12x 28,351,488B fp32; b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b: 1x 157,541,376B fp32, the last-ready bucket holding the tied wte/lm_head, wpe, ln_f and h.0.ln_1 gradients). This is the same boundary the previous trial-8469963975 used, whose structure passed quality, coverage and the math-policy checks, so the region is a proven-coherent editable boundary; only its execution policy failed. Measured facts motivating the opportunity: the objective baseline is 53.63 ms (max-rank median of the original baseline; rank 1: 53.63, rank 0: 36.00), while the wire cost of the frozen 497,759,232-byte fp32 gradient payload is only ~33-35 ms, measured three independent ways: aligned synthetic calibration (2.00 ms per 28,351,488B, 10.63 ms per 157,541,376B, ~14.2-14.8 GB/s effective payload rate), the non-waiting rank in the current execution timeline (12x ~1.9 ms + 10.59 ms = 33.4 ms), and the previous trial's single fused allreduce (33.12 ms clean diagnostic; 33.32/33.46 ms under nsys). The remaining ~19 ms on the official diagnostic's max rank (and ~10 ms on rank 0 in the timeline capture - the waiting direction flips between captures) is in-kernel device waiting from rank-arrival skew, not transfer: the early rank submits each bucket allreduce as soon as its own bucket is ready and its NCCL kernels spin until the peer arrives (first kernel +3.5 ms, then ~0.7 ms per subsequent kernel in the timeline; rank-0 ~13.9 ms vs rank-1 ~1.86 ms per collective in discovery). Concrete previous failure to repair: trial-8469963975 fused the whole gradient set into one barrier-aligned allreduce issued only after backward completed (plus pack, cuda sync and unpack on the critical path). It reached the communication floor (33.12 ms, samples 33.05/33.12/33.46) but was rejected solely on the step_ms constraint: 127.07 ms vs the 120.90 ms limit (1.05 x 115.14), because it gave up the reducer's overlap: in the baseline timeline the 13-bucket collective pipeline runs +139.3 -> +185.0 ms while the 4th microbatch's backward runs ~+135 -> +168.4 ms, so only ~16.5 ms of communication is exposed after backward ends, whereas the fused route exposed the entire ~33 ms plus ~4 ms of pack/barrier/unpack. The repair is therefore a synchronization-scheduling change inside this region: keep NCCL submissions rank-aligned CPU-side so kernel durations stay at wire cost, but launch the gradient collectives progressively as gradient groups become final during the final microbatch's backward, restoring the parent's overlap. Alternatives are closed: the 25 MiB DDP bucketing is built by the frozen adapter's prepare(); shrinking the fp32 payload is barred by exact cross-rank equality (atol=0) and the 1e-6/1e-4 reference tolerances; NCCL algorithm/protocol environment changes are provider configuration and cannot take effect after prepare() has already initialized the process group; compute-kernel groups (aten::mm/addmm, ~10.7 ms diagnostic) do not move the NCCL-kernel objective.
selection.hypothesis: Replace project.invoke with a step that, once per process, installs a gradient-synchronization policy on the existing DDP wrapper (state['model']) and otherwise runs the parent's workload unchanged: the same zero_grad, four no_sync microbatches, final synchronized backward, SGD step and synchronize. The policy replaces the default reducer's bucket allreduces (the two observed c10d::allreduce_ sites) with collectives that (a) fire progressively, per bucket or in 4-6 fused chunks, at the moment each gradient group becomes final during the 4th microbatch's backward - preserving the measured baseline launch schedule (first launch ~4 ms into that backward, ~29 ms of the ~34 ms wire hidden under remaining backward compute) - and (b) before each NCCL submission, align the ranks with a barrier on the existing gloo control group, which blocks CPU-side only, emits no NCCL kernels, and was already accepted inside the timed step by the previous trial, so the 10-20 ms of run-direction-dependent skew is absorbed as CPU wait on the early rank (which has slack; its wall was already paced by the late rank) instead of as NCCL kernel spin. The reduction keeps the default reducer's arithmetic (SUM then divide by world_size on the same bucket buffers, gradient_as_bucket_view), so per-element results are bitwise identical to the baseline for world_size 2 - a single commutative fp32 add regardless of chunk fusion - and the previous trial already demonstrated that even a fully fused variant passes the exact cross-rank check, the serial-reference gradient/parameter tolerances and the negative control. Expected, to be tested: diagnostic.max_rank_nccl_kernel_sum_ms drops from 53.63 to ~34-38 ms (floor ~33-35 ms = measured wire cost; residual = launch-side gaps after alignment), i.e. a >=30% reduction, while step_ms stays at ~116-120 ms, within the 120.90 ms constraint: the late rank's critical path gains only ~13 barrier calls of ~0.1-0.3 ms plus Python hook dispatch (mitigated to ~1-2 ms by fusing into 4-6 chunks with ~1 ms of chunk pack/unpack copies), versus the +11.9 ms serialization regression of the previous fused design. Quality, coverage and the math policy are expected unchanged. Fallbacks if measured otherwise: reduce alignment points (fewer, larger chunks) if step_ms exceeds 120.90; increase alignment granularity if residual in-kernel waiting leaves the metric above ~40 ms. Known risk to monitor: one flaky 385.8 ms rank-1 clean sample appeared in the previous trial; the alignment path must not add per-step variance, and median aggregation over the 3 diagnostic invocations and 5 clean repeats is the acceptance filter, not any single sample.

selection.rationale: Objective is the per-rank summed NCCL device-kernel duration, max across ranks, median over 3 separately profiled steps: baseline samples [54.868, 40.490, 53.625] ms (rank 1 [54.87, 40.49, 53.63] vs rank 0 [35.73, 36.03, 36.00]). All communication in the step is 13 f32 SUM allreduces on the default NCCL group (12x 28,351,488 B buckets + 1x 157,541,376 B bucket = 497,759,232 B), dispatched by the DDP reducer during the last microbatch's backward; both allreduce call records (d0938de87369efd500322679, 12 invocations; b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b, 1 invocation) are children of the project invoke call 5d7d6bb13691b02f533f62b0. Measured both-peers-ready references (collective_calibration, separate warmed worker): ~1.99-2.01 ms per 28.35 MB and ~10.58-10.63 ms per 157.5 MB collective, i.e. a wire floor of about 34.6 ms for the step's bytes; bytes themselves are not reducible because gradients must stay fp32, bit-identical across ranks and reference-matched. Rank 0's clean kernel sum (~36.0 ms) already sits ~1.4 ms above that floor, while the max rank carries 6-19 ms of in-kernel spin waiting (rank 1 in the clean baseline; rank 0 in the independent execution_timeline capture, 45.6 vs 35.6 ms; rank 0's 196.1 ms in the perturbed discovery capture is not used quantitatively). The waiting mass is created by the baseline schedule: no_sync on 3 of 4 microbatches and 13 per-bucket collectives interleaved into a CPU-launch-bound eager backward produce 13 rank-arrival sync points (compute overlap measured at only 7.7-11.3 ms of the 45.6 ms comm union). The coherent editable boundary is therefore the complete accumulated-step region (project invoke) plus the two nested allreduce groups it owns: rewrite the step so gradient synchronization executes once, after all backward compute, as a single fused allreduce over a flat fp32 copy of the locally accumulated gradients (pre-divide by world_size, SUM on the default NCCL group, in-place copy back into .grad before optimizer.step), with the DDP reducer left idle via no_sync on all 4 microbatches. Per-element arithmetic stays identical to the DDP default hook (divide by world_size then SUM), preserving exact cross-rank gradient equality (atol=0, rtol=0), the serial global-batch reference and post-step parameter checks; zero_grad stays inside the timed region and the only collectives in the clean timing path remain the step's own real NCCL gradient synchronization.
selection.hypothesis: Replacing 13 interleaved bucket allreduces with one post-backward fused 497,759,232 B collective removes ~12 rank-arrival sync events (measured max-rank excess over the both-peers-ready floor implies ~0.9-1.5 ms of accumulated spin per sync point) and 12 per-collective ramp/drain/launch overheads, so the diagnostic max-rank kernel-sum should fall from 53.6 ms toward the wire floor, plausibly to ~35-38 ms (~30% reduction) with lower sample variance (baseline spread 40.5-54.9 ms). Treated as unproven: a fused 497 MB collective was never observed (extrapolated from the measured ~14.2-14.8 GB/s logical payload rate at the two observed sizes); arrival skew at the single remaining sync point could still show a tail event, though bounded by one skew sample instead of 13; and the step_ms constraint has only ~5.8 ms headroom (<=1.05x the 115.1 ms median-of-max) because the rewrite forfeits the measured 7.7-11.3 ms of comm/compute overlap while removing the waiting rank's in-kernel spin - net wall-clock and objective effect must be verified by measurement, including the fp32 flat-buffer copy traffic (~1-2 ms) and unchanged correctness/negative-control outcomes.
